attributes.description: Percentage of time the transport asset is actively deployed in operations versus idle or available time. Key performance indicator (KPI) for fleet efficiency and return on investment (ROI).

attributes.name: vin_serial_number
attributes.description: Unique vehicle identification number (VIN) for road vehicles or manufacturer serial number for aircraft, vessels, and rail units. Used for registration, insurance, and theft prevention.
attributes.references: US Department of Transportation (DOT), International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO)

attributes.name: volume_capacity_cbm
attributes.description: Maximum volumetric capacity in cubic meters (CBM) that the transport asset can accommodate. Used for space optimization and dimensional weight (DIM weight) calculations.

attributes.name: width_meters
attributes.description: Physical width of the transport asset in meters. Used for route clearance and infrastructure compatibility assessment.

attributes.name: year_of_manufacture
attributes.description: Calendar year when the transport asset was manufactured or built. Used for age-based maintenance scheduling and regulatory compliance.
attributes.references: US Department of Transportation (DOT), International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO)

products.name: container_unit
products.description: Master record for intermodal containers and unit load devices (ULDs) managed within the fleet. Tracks container number (ISO 6346), TEU size classification (20ft, 40ft, 45ft), container type (dry, reefer, open-top, flat-rack, tank), tare weight, max gross weight, CSC certification expiry, current location (port/depot/vessel), availability status, lease agreement reference, and last inspection date. Distinct from transport_asset as containers are cargo-carrying units with their own ISO standards and lifecycle separate from traction units.

attributes.name: container_unit_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the container unit. Primary key for the container_unit data product.

attributes.name: agreement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to contract.agreement. Business justification: Container lease management: container_unit.lease_agreement_reference is a denormalized text reference to a contract agreement. Replacing with a proper FK enables lease cost tracking, expiry management

attributes.name: asset_type_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to fleet.asset_type. Business justification: container_unit currently has container_type (STRING) storing the container classification as free text. Containers are a category of fleet assets and should reference the asset_type taxonomy. The asse

attributes.name: carrier_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to network.carrier. Business justification: Container repatriation, detention/demurrage billing, and carrier asset pool management require knowing which carrier owns or leases each container unit. Logistics domain experts universally expect con

attributes.name: current_depot_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to fleet.depot. Business justification: Containers have a current location (current_location_type, current_location_code). When a container is at a fleet depot, this FK provides a structured link. Nullable because containers can be at ports

attributes.name: current_location_network_node_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Current Location Network Node Id (Foreign Key)
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to route.network_node. Business justification: container_unit.current_location_code is a denormalized plain-text field. Normalizing to network_node enables container tracking, node-level inventory reporting, and repositioning optimization — core c

attributes.name: lane_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to route.lane. Business justification: Container positioning and repositioning decisions are made at the trade-lane level. Knowing which lane a container is currently assigned to is fundamental to container fleet management and empty repos

attributes.name: manufacturer_supplier_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to procurement.supplier. Business justification: Container OEM supplier linkage: normalizes the plain 'manufacturer' text field to the procurement supplier master, enabling warranty claims, CSC certification follow-up with the OEM, and parts sourcin

attributes.name: purchase_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to procurement.purchase_order. Business justification: Container acquisition procurement: containers are capital assets purchased via POs. Linking container_unit to its originating PO supports warranty tracking, CSC certification cost allocation, and asse

attributes.name: acquisition_cost
attributes.description: Total cost paid to acquire the container, including purchase price or initial lease payment. Used for CAPEX tracking, asset valuation, and return on investment analysis.
attributes.references: IFRS 16 - Leases; Internal Financial Reporting Standards

attributes.name: acquisition_date
attributes.description: Date the container was acquired by the company (purchase or lease commencement). Used for asset tracking, depreciation schedules, and fleet age analysis.

attributes.name: availability_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of the container. Available for booking, in use on a shipment, in transit empty, under repair/maintenance, retired from service, or lost/missing. Critical for inventory management and booking systems.

attributes.name: condition_grade
attributes.description: Physical condition assessment of the container. Grade A (excellent, cargo-worthy), B (good, minor wear), C (fair, requires monitoring), D (poor, repair needed), Scrap (end of life). Determines suitability for cargo types and repair priority.
attributes.references: Institute of International Container Lessors (IICL) - Container Inspection Criteria

attributes.name: container_number
attributes.description: Unique container identification number following ISO 6346 standard format (4 letter owner code + 6 digit serial number + 1 check digit). This is the globally recognized identifier for the container unit.
attributes.references: ISO 6346 - Freight containers - Coding, identification and marking

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this container unit record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: csc_certification_date
attributes.description: Date the current CSC safety certification was issued. Used to track certification validity and schedule re-inspection.
attributes.references: IMO - International Convention for Safe Containers (CSC)

attributes.name: csc_certification_number
attributes.description: Unique certification number issued under the International Convention for Safe Containers (CSC). Certifies the container meets structural safety standards for international transport.
attributes.references: IMO - International Convention for Safe Containers (CSC)

attributes.name: csc_expiry_date
attributes.description: Expiration date of the CSC safety certification. Containers must be re-inspected and re-certified before this date to remain in service. Non-compliance prevents international movement.
attributes.references: IMO - International Convention for Safe Containers (CSC)

attributes.name: current_book_value
attributes.description: Current accounting book value of the container after depreciation. Updated periodically based on depreciation schedule. Used for financial reporting and asset disposal decisions.
attributes.references: IFRS 16 - Leases; IAS 16 - Property, Plant and Equipment

attributes.name: current_location_country
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO country code of the containers current location. Used for geographic fleet distribution analysis and repositioning planning.

attributes.name: current_location_type
attributes.description: Type of facility or mode where the container is currently located. Depot (storage yard), port (marine terminal), vessel (on ship), rail yard, customer site, or in transit between locations.

attributes.name: disposal_date
attributes.description: Date the container was disposed of (sold, scrapped, or otherwise removed from company ownership). Null if still owned. Used for asset lifecycle closure and financial reconciliation.

attributes.name: food_grade_certified
attributes.description: Indicates whether the container is certified for transporting food products, meeting hygiene and contamination prevention standards. True if food-grade certified, false otherwise.
attributes.references: FDA Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA); EU Regulation (EC) No 852/2004 on the hygiene of foodstuffs

attributes.name: gps_enabled
attributes.description: Indicates whether the container is equipped with GPS tracking device for real-time location monitoring. True if GPS-enabled, false otherwise.
attributes.references: Internal IoT (Internet of Things) Fleet Tracking System

attributes.name: hazmat_certified
attributes.description: Indicates whether the container is certified to carry hazardous materials (dangerous goods) per IMDG Code and ICAO Technical Instructions. True if certified, false otherwise.
attributes.references: IMO - International Maritime Dangerous Goods (IMDG) Code; ICAO - Technical Instructions for the Safe Transport of Dangerous Goods by Air

attributes.name: height_ft
attributes.description: External height of the container in feet. Standard height is 8.5 feet; high-cube containers are 9.5 feet. Determines stacking compatibility and clearance requirements.
attributes.references: ISO 668 - Series 1 freight containers - Classification, dimensions and ratings

attributes.name: internal_volume_cbm
attributes.description: Internal cargo capacity of the container in cubic meters (CBM). Used for volumetric load planning and dimensional weight calculations.
attributes.references: ISO 668 - Series 1 freight containers - Classification, dimensions and ratings

attributes.name: last_inspection_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent physical inspection of the container. Inspections verify structural integrity, door seals, flooring, and compliance with safety standards.
attributes.references: IICL - Container Inspection Criteria; Internal Maintenance Policy

attributes.name: last_maintenance_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent maintenance or repair work performed on the container. Tracks maintenance history and informs future service intervals.

attributes.name: last_movement_date
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent movement or position update for the container. Used for tracking, dwell time calculation, and real-time visibility.
attributes.references: Internal TMS (Transportation Management System); FourKites Real-Time Visibility Platform

attributes.name: length_ft
attributes.description: External length of the container in feet. Standard sizes are 10, 20, 40, 45, 48, or 53 feet. Critical for transport planning, stacking, and terminal slot allocation.
attributes.references: ISO 668 - Series 1 freight containers - Classification, dimensions and ratings

attributes.name: manufacture_date
attributes.description: Date the container was manufactured. Used to calculate asset age, depreciation, and remaining useful life for maintenance and replacement planning.
attributes.references: ISO 6346 - Freight containers - Coding, identification and marking

attributes.name: max_gross_weight_kg
attributes.description: Maximum permissible combined weight of the container and its cargo in kilograms. Enforced for safety, regulatory compliance (SOLAS VGM), and transport mode restrictions.
attributes.references: ISO 668 - Series 1 freight containers - Classification, dimensions and ratings; SOLAS Convention Verified Gross Mass (VGM)

attributes.name: max_payload_kg
attributes.description: Maximum cargo weight the container can carry, calculated as max gross weight minus tare weight. Used for load planning and customer quoting.
attributes.references: ISO 668 - Series 1 freight containers - Classification, dimensions and ratings

attributes.name: next_inspection_due_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next mandatory inspection. Used for preventive maintenance planning and compliance tracking.
attributes.references: IICL - Container Inspection Criteria; Internal Maintenance Policy

attributes.name: owner_code
attributes.description: Four-letter code identifying the container owner or operator, as registered with the Bureau International des Containers (BIC). First three letters identify the owner; fourth letter is the equipment category (U for freight container).
attributes.references: ISO 6346 - Freight containers - Coding, identification and marking; BIC (Bureau International des Containers)

attributes.name: ownership_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether the container is owned by the carrier, leased from a lessor, owned by a customer (SOC - Shipper Owned Container), or part of a shared pool arrangement. Impacts cost allocation, maintenance responsibility, and repositioning strategy.

attributes.name: reefer_capable
attributes.description: Indicates whether the container has refrigeration capability for temperature-controlled cargo. True for reefer containers, false for dry and other non-refrigerated types.
attributes.references: ISO 1496-2 - Series 1 freight containers - Specification and testing - Part 2: Thermal containers

attributes.name: retirement_date
attributes.description: Date the container was retired from active service. Null if the container is still in service. Used for fleet lifecycle management and disposal tracking.

attributes.name: rfid_tag_code
attributes.description: Unique identifier of the RFID tag attached to the container for automated tracking at gates, terminals, and checkpoints. Null if container is not RFID-tagged.
attributes.references: ISO 17363 - Supply chain applications of RFID - Freight containers; ISO 17365 - Supply chain applications of RFID - Transport units

attributes.name: tare_weight_kg
attributes.description: Empty weight of the container in kilograms, excluding cargo. Used to calculate net cargo weight and verify compliance with gross weight limits.
attributes.references: ISO 668 - Series 1 freight containers - Classification, dimensions and ratings

attributes.name: temperature_range_max_c
attributes.description: Maximum temperature the container can maintain in Celsius. Applicable only to refrigerated (reefer) containers. Null for non-reefer units.
attributes.references: ISO 1496-2 - Series 1 freight containers - Specification and testing - Part 2: Thermal containers

attributes.name: temperature_range_min_c
attributes.description: Minimum temperature the container can maintain in Celsius. Applicable only to refrigerated (reefer) containers. Null for non-reefer units.
attributes.references: ISO 1496-2 - Series 1 freight containers - Specification and testing - Part 2: Thermal containers

attributes.name: teu_size
attributes.description: Container size expressed in TEU (Twenty-foot Equivalent Unit). Standard values: 1.0 for 20ft, 2.0 for 40ft, 2.25 for 45ft. Used for capacity planning and vessel/terminal utilization calculations.
attributes.references: ISO 668 - Series 1 freight containers - Classification, dimensions and ratings

attributes.name: total_distance_km
attributes.description: Cumulative distance the container has traveled in kilometers since acquisition. Used for wear analysis, maintenance scheduling, and asset performance evaluation.
attributes.references: Internal Fleet Management System; GPS Telematics

attributes.name: total_trips_completed
attributes.description: Cumulative count of completed shipment trips (loaded movements) the container has performed since acquisition. Used for utilization analysis and lifecycle tracking.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this container unit record was last modified. Used for audit trail, change tracking, and data freshness monitoring.

attributes.name: width_ft
attributes.description: External width of the container in feet. Standard width is 8.0 feet; high-cube and specialized containers may be 8.5 feet.
attributes.references: ISO 668 - Series 1 freight containers - Classification, dimensions and ratings

products.name: asset_assignment
products.description: Transactional record capturing the assignment of a transport asset (vehicle, aircraft, vessel) to a specific route, freight order, driver, or operational depot for a defined period. Tracks assignment type (route execution, depot standby, charter, maintenance hold), assigned driver/crew reference, origin depot, destination, planned start/end datetime, actual start/end datetime, TMS freight order reference, and assignment status. Enables fleet utilization tracking and TMS-to-fleet reconciliation.

attributes.name: asset_assignment_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the asset assignment record. Primary key for the asset assignment transaction.

attributes.name: agreement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to contract.agreement. Business justification: Asset assignments execute contracted service commitments. Operations teams validate assignment compliance with customer/carrier agreements for rate validation, SLA tracking, and billing reconciliation

attributes.name: carrier_agreement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to contract.carrier_agreement. Business justification: Carrier performance and liability management: when assets are assigned under carrier agreements, the specific carrier agreement governs liability limits, EDI requirements, and capacity terms. This lin

attributes.name: carrier_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to network.carrier. Business justification: Asset assignments frequently use external carriers for line-haul or last-mile segments. Carrier selection, performance tracking, cost allocation, and SLA compliance depend on this link. Essential for

attributes.name: carrier_payable_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to billing.carrier_payable. Business justification: Asset assignments involving third-party carriers generate carrier payables for the service leg. Linking asset_assignment to carrier_payable enables freight cost management, carrier payment reconciliat

attributes.name: carrier_service_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to network.carrier_service. Business justification: Asset assignments fulfill specific carrier service bookings (ocean service, rail service, air service). Linking asset_assignment to carrier_service enables service-level capacity utilization reporting

attributes.name: customer_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to customer.customer_account. Business justification: Dedicated fleet contracts require asset assignments to be linked to a customer account for customer-specific utilization reporting, dedicated fleet billing, and SLA performance tracking. Logistics ope

attributes.name: customs_declaration_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to customs.declaration. Business justification: Asset assignments (trips/jobs) involving cross-border freight require customs declarations. Links operational dispatch to regulatory compliance, supports driver briefings on customs requirements, and

attributes.name: destination_depot_id
attributes.description: Reference to the depot, terminal, or facility where the assignment is scheduled to end. The ending location for the asset assignment. Null for open-ended assignments such as depot standby. Links to warehouse or facility master data.

attributes.name: dispute_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to billing.billing_dispute. Business justification: Billing disputes frequently arise from specific asset assignments where charges don't match contracted rates or actual service delivered. Linking asset_assignment to billing_dispute enables dispute re

attributes.name: driver_profile_id
attributes.description: Reference to the driver or crew member assigned to operate the asset during this assignment. Null for uncrewed assignments such as container assignments or depot standby. Links to workforce driver master data.
attributes.references: US Department of Transportation (DOT) - Driver Qualification Files

attributes.name: freight_audit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to billing.freight_audit. Business justification: Freight audit validates carrier charges against the actual assignment executed (contracted vs invoiced weight, distance, accessorials). Linking asset_assignment to freight_audit is essential for freig

attributes.name: freight_order_id
attributes.description: Reference to the TMS freight order that this asset is assigned to execute. Null for non-route assignments such as depot standby or maintenance hold. Enables TMS-to-fleet reconciliation.

attributes.name: lane_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to route.lane. Business justification: Lane-level asset deployment reporting (which assets run which lanes, utilization by lane) is a core fleet planning process. asset_assignment links to plan but not directly to lane; direct FK enables l

attributes.name: origin_depot_id
attributes.description: Reference to the depot, terminal, or facility where the assignment originates. The starting location for the asset assignment. Links to warehouse or facility master data.

attributes.name: pickup_facility_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to warehouse.facility. Business justification: Asset assignments for warehouse pickup/delivery operations must reference the specific warehouse facility being serviced. This enables facility-level fleet utilization reporting, dock capacity plannin

attributes.name: plan_id
attributes.description: Reference to the planned route that the asset is assigned to execute. Applicable for route execution assignments. Links to route master data for origin, destination, and waypoints.

attributes.name: rate_card_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to pricing.rate_card. Business justification: Asset assignments execute freight movements billed under a specific rate card. Logistics billing and revenue recognition require knowing which rate card governed each assignment. Dispatchers and finan

attributes.name: rate_schedule_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to contract.rate_schedule. Business justification: Assignment cost validation: asset assignments incur costs governed by contracted rate schedules. Linking assignment to rate_schedule enables cost-per-assignment validation against contracted rates, su

attributes.name: service_scope_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to contract.service_scope. Business justification: Contractual service compliance: asset assignments must comply with the contracted service scope (hazmat authorization, temperature control, geographic limits). This link enables real-time compliance c

attributes.name: shipment_leg_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to shipment.shipment_leg. Business justification: An asset assignment executes a specific shipment leg. Fleet dispatchers need to know which shipment leg an asset assignment is fulfilling for SLA monitoring, cost allocation per leg, and operational r

attributes.name: shipper_profile_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to customer.shipper_profile. Business justification: Shipper profiles contain hazmat certifications, temperature requirements, and special handling instructions that directly govern which assets can be assigned for a shipper's cargo. Compliance and safe

attributes.name: sla_commitment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to contract.contract_sla_commitment. Business justification: Real-time SLA breach detection: each asset assignment is measured against a specific SLA commitment (OTD, OTIF, transit time). This link enables automated SLA compliance tracking at the assignment lev

attributes.name: sla_entitlement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to customer.sla_entitlement. Business justification: Premium logistics customers have SLA entitlements (guaranteed transit times, priority handling) that must govern asset assignment decisions. Fleet dispatchers reference the SLA entitlement to assign a

attributes.name: transport_asset_id
attributes.description: Reference to the transport asset (vehicle, aircraft, vessel, container) being assigned. Links to the fleet asset master data.

attributes.name: trip_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to fleet.trip. Business justification: Asset assignments represent the allocation of a transport asset to an operational run. Linking to trip provides the trip-level context. fleet_driver_assignment already has trip_id; asset_assignment sh

attributes.name: actual_end_datetime
attributes.description: Actual date and time when the asset assignment ended. Captured from GPS telematics, RFID tag reads, or manual check-out. Used for On-Time In-Full (OTIF) performance measurement and variance analysis against planned end. Null for in-progress assignments.

attributes.name: actual_start_datetime
attributes.description: Actual date and time when the asset assignment began. Captured from GPS telematics, RFID tag reads, or manual check-in. Used for On-Time Departure (OTD) performance measurement and variance analysis against planned start.

attributes.name: assignment_cost_amount
attributes.description: Total operational cost incurred for this assignment including fuel, driver wages, tolls, and maintenance. Used for OPEX tracking, profitability analysis, and cost-per-kilometer KPI calculation. Captured in the companys base currency.

attributes.name: assignment_duration_hours
attributes.description: Planned or actual duration of the assignment in hours. Used for fleet utilization KPI calculation, driver hours-of-service compliance, and asset availability forecasting. Calculated from start and end datetimes.
attributes.references: US Department of Transportation (DOT) - Hours of Service Regulations

attributes.name: assignment_number
attributes.description: Business-readable unique identifier for the assignment, typically generated by the Transportation Management System (TMS). Used for operational tracking and communication.

attributes.name: assignment_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the assignment. Planned indicates scheduled but not confirmed, confirmed for approved assignments, in progress for active assignments, completed for finished assignments, cancelled for voided assignments, suspended for temporarily halted assignments, failed for assignments that could not be completed. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: planned|confirmed|in_progress|completed|cancelled|suspended|failed — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: assignment_type
attributes.description: Classification of the assignment purpose. Route execution indicates active transport duty, depot standby for available assets, charter for third-party rental, maintenance hold for scheduled service, repair for unscheduled fixes, inspection for regulatory checks, lease out for external rental, reserve for contingency, training for crew qualification, emergency deployment for urgent needs. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: route_execution|depot_standby|charter|maintenance_hold|repair|inspection|lease_out|reserve|training|emergency_deployment — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: cargo_volume_cbm
attributes.description: Total volume of cargo loaded on the asset during this assignment in cubic meters. Used for capacity utilization analysis and dimensional weight (DIM weight) calculations. Null for non-cargo assignments.
attributes.references: International Air Transport Association (IATA) - Cargo Measurement Standards

attributes.name: cargo_weight_kg
attributes.description: Total weight of cargo loaded on the asset during this assignment in kilograms. Used for load optimization, weight compliance checks, and fuel consumption correlation analysis. Null for non-cargo assignments.
attributes.references: International Maritime Organization (IMO) - SOLAS Weight Verification

attributes.name: co2_emissions_kg
attributes.business_glossary_term: Carbon Dioxide Equivalent (CO2e) Emissions in Kilograms (kg)
attributes.description: Total greenhouse gas emissions in kilograms of CO2 equivalent produced during this assignment. Calculated from fuel consumption using emission factors. Used for sustainability reporting, EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) compliance, and Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA) reporting.
attributes.references: ISO 14064 - Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Accounting and Verification

attributes.name: compliance_check_status
attributes.description: Status of regulatory compliance checks for this assignment including DOT inspections, ICAO airworthiness, IMO safety checks, and customs pre-clearance. Passed indicates all checks cleared, failed for violations, pending for in-progress checks, not required for exempt assignments, waived for authorized exceptions.
attributes.references: US Department of Transportation (DOT) - Compliance and Enforcement

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this assignment record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail, data lineage tracking, and record lifecycle management. Automatically populated by the system.

attributes.name: cross_border_indicator
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the assignment involves crossing international borders requiring customs clearance and trade compliance. True for international assignments, false for domestic.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the assignment cost amount. Typically the companys base operating currency (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP).

attributes.name: delay_duration_minutes
attributes.description: Total duration of delays in minutes. Calculated as the difference between planned and actual completion times. Used for Service Level Agreement (SLA) compliance measurement and root cause analysis. Zero if no delay occurred.

attributes.name: delay_reason_code
attributes.description: Standardized code indicating the primary reason for any delay in completing the assignment. Weather for adverse conditions, traffic for congestion, mechanical for breakdowns, customs for clearance delays, loading delay for shipper delays, driver unavailable for crew issues, route change for diversions, accident for incidents, other for miscellaneous, none if no delay occurred. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: weather|traffic|mechanical|customs|loading_delay|driver_unavailable|route_change|accident|other|none — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: distance_km
attributes.description: Planned or actual distance covered during the assignment in kilometers. Used for fuel consumption analysis, maintenance scheduling based on mileage, and route optimization. Captured from GPS telematics or route planning systems.
attributes.references: ISO 80000-3 - Quantities and Units of Space and Time

attributes.name: fuel_consumed_liters
attributes.description: Actual fuel consumed during the assignment in liters. Captured from vehicle telematics, fuel card transactions, or manual fuel logs. Used for OPEX tracking, Carbon Dioxide Equivalent (CO2e) emissions calculation, and fuel efficiency KPIs.
attributes.references: ISO 14064 - Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Accounting and Verification

attributes.name: gps_tracking_enabled
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether real-time GPS tracking is enabled for this assignment. True if telematics data is being captured, false otherwise. Used for real-time visibility and predictive ETA calculation.

attributes.name: hazmat_indicator
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the assignment involves transport of hazardous materials requiring special handling, placarding, and regulatory compliance. True if hazmat cargo is present, false otherwise.
attributes.references: IMDG Code - International Maritime Dangerous Goods Code

attributes.name: incident_reported_indicator
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether any incident (accident, breakdown, delay, cargo damage, security breach) was reported during this assignment. True if an incident occurred, false otherwise. Links to incident or claims management systems.

attributes.name: last_inspection_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent regulatory or safety inspection performed on the asset prior to or during this assignment. Used for compliance tracking and maintenance scheduling. Null if no inspection has been performed.

attributes.name: load_utilization_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage of the assets maximum capacity utilized during this assignment. Calculated as (actual cargo weight or volume / maximum capacity) * 100. Key performance indicator for fleet efficiency and load optimization.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this assignment record was last modified. Used for audit trail, change tracking, and data synchronization. Automatically updated by the system on any change.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for operational notes, special instructions, or comments related to the assignment. Used for communication between dispatchers, drivers, and operations teams. May include handling instructions, customer requirements, or incident details.

attributes.name: planned_end_datetime
attributes.description: Scheduled date and time when the asset assignment is planned to end. Used for capacity planning and turnaround time calculation. Corresponds to Estimated Time of Arrival (ETA) for route assignments. Null for open-ended assignments.

attributes.name: planned_start_datetime
attributes.description: Scheduled date and time when the asset assignment is planned to begin. Used for capacity planning and resource scheduling. Corresponds to Estimated Time of Departure (ETD) for route assignments.

attributes.name: priority_level
attributes.description: Business priority of the assignment. Critical for time-sensitive or high-value shipments, high for express delivery, normal for standard service, low for deferred or backhaul assignments. Influences resource allocation and scheduling decisions.

attributes.name: rfid_tag_code
attributes.description: Unique identifier of the RFID tag attached to the asset for automated tracking and identification. Used for gate-in/gate-out automation, asset location tracking, and inventory management. Null if RFID is not used.

attributes.name: seal_number
attributes.description: Unique identifier of the security seal applied to the asset (container, trailer, or cargo compartment) to ensure cargo integrity and prevent tampering. Required for customs compliance and high-security shipments. Null if no seal is applied.

attributes.name: service_level
attributes.description: Service level agreement (SLA) tier for this assignment. Express for next-day or same-day delivery, standard for 2-5 day delivery, economy for 5+ day delivery, charter for exclusive use, dedicated for contract logistics. Determines performance targets and pricing.

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the operational system of record that originated this assignment. SAP TM for SAP Transportation Management, ORACLE TMS for Oracle Transportation Management System, MANHATTAN WMS for warehouse-initiated assignments, FOURKITES for visibility platform assignments, MANUAL for manually created assignments, OTHER for miscellaneous sources. Used for data lineage and system integration tracking.

attributes.name: temperature_controlled_indicator
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the assignment requires temperature-controlled transport (refrigerated or heated). True for cold chain or temperature-sensitive cargo, false otherwise.

products.name: telematics_event
products.description: High-frequency IoT/GPS telemetry event records streamed from onboard telematics devices fitted to fleet assets. Captures asset ID, device ID, event timestamp (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX), GPS coordinates (latitude, longitude, altitude), speed, heading, odometer reading, engine RPM, fuel level, ignition state, harsh braking/acceleration flags, geofence entry/exit events, temperature sensor readings (for reefer units), and raw IoT payload reference. Sourced from FourKites real-time visibility platform. Enables predictive ETA, route deviation detection, and driver behavior scoring.
products.reference: FourKites GPS Telemetry / IoT Sensor Feed

attributes.name: telematics_event_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the telematics event record. Primary key for the telematics event stream.

attributes.name: carrier_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to network.carrier. Business justification: When assets are operated by contracted carriers, telematics events must track carrier for liability determination, performance monitoring (speed, idling, route adherence), and billing reconciliation.

attributes.name: consignment_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the active shipment being transported by the asset at the time of the event. Links telemetry to freight orders for predictive ETA and exception management.
attributes.references: SAP TM, FourKites Real-Time Visibility Platform

attributes.name: driver_profile_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the driver assigned to the asset at the time of the event. Used for driver behavior scoring, hours-of-service compliance, and workforce analytics.

attributes.name: priority
attributes.description: Business priority level assigned to the maintenance order, determining urgency and resource allocation (critical for safety or operational impact, high for near-term service impact, medium for scheduled work, low for deferred maintenance).

attributes.name: raised_date
attributes.description: The date when the maintenance order was first created or raised in the system, representing the business event timestamp when the need for maintenance was identified.

attributes.name: regulatory_inspection_type
attributes.description: Type of regulatory or statutory inspection performed as part of this maintenance order: dot_annual (DOT annual vehicle inspection), icao_airworthiness (ICAO airworthiness check), maritime_survey (vessel classification survey), emissions_test (environmental compliance test), safety_certification (safety system certification), none (not a regulatory inspection).
attributes.references: DOT Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations, ICAO Annex 8 Airworthiness, IMO International Maritime Organization

attributes.name: scheduled_completion_date
attributes.description: The planned date when maintenance work is expected to be completed and the asset returned to service, used for operational planning and customer commitments.

attributes.name: scheduled_start_date
attributes.description: The planned date when maintenance work is scheduled to begin, used for resource planning and asset availability forecasting.

attributes.name: total_maintenance_cost
attributes.description: Total cost of the maintenance order including parts, labor, external services, and any other direct costs, representing the complete OPEX impact of this maintenance event for financial reporting and asset lifecycle costing.

attributes.name: warranty_claim_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator whether this maintenance order is associated with a warranty claim against the asset manufacturer or component supplier, used for cost recovery tracking.

attributes.name: warranty_claim_number
attributes.description: Reference number for the associated warranty claim submitted to the manufacturer or supplier, applicable when warranty_claim_flag is true.

attributes.name: work_order_number
attributes.description: Externally-known unique business identifier for the maintenance work order, used for tracking and reference across systems and with external vendors.

attributes.name: work_performed_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative of the actual maintenance work performed, including procedures followed, parts replaced, adjustments made, and test results, completed upon work order closure.

products.name: maintenance_schedule
products.description: Master record defining the preventive maintenance schedule and service intervals for each fleet asset type. Captures asset type, service type (oil change, tyre rotation, brake inspection, DOT annual inspection, ICAO 100-hour check), trigger basis (mileage interval, engine hours, calendar days), next due mileage/hours/date, last completed date, compliance mandatory flag, regulatory body (DOT, ICAO, IMO), and schedule status. Drives automated maintenance_order generation and ensures regulatory compliance with DOT, ICAO, and IMO inspection requirements.
products.reference: OEM Service Manual / DOT Inspection Schedule

attributes.name: maintenance_schedule_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the maintenance schedule record. Primary key.

attributes.name: maintenance_facility_id
attributes.description: Reference to the maintenance facility, depot, or service center where this maintenance is scheduled to be performed.

attributes.name: supplier_id
attributes.description: Reference to the preferred maintenance vendor or service provider for this scheduled maintenance. Null if performed in-house.

attributes.name: transport_asset_id
attributes.description: Reference to the fleet asset (vehicle, aircraft, vessel, container) to which this maintenance schedule applies.

attributes.name: auto_generate_order_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the system should automatically generate a maintenance work order when the schedule trigger conditions are met (True) or require manual creation (False).

attributes.name: compliance_mandatory_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this maintenance schedule is mandated by regulatory compliance requirements (True) or is discretionary preventive maintenance (False).
attributes.references: US DOT FMCSA Regulations, ICAO Annex 6, IMO SOLAS

attributes.name: cost_currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the estimated cost (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this maintenance schedule record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: downtime_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the asset must be taken out of service (True) or can remain operational during maintenance (False).

attributes.name: estimated_cost
attributes.description: Estimated total cost in base currency for completing this scheduled maintenance service, including labor and parts.

attributes.name: estimated_duration_hours
attributes.description: Estimated time in hours required to complete this maintenance service.

attributes.name: interval_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the maintenance interval value (miles, kilometers, engine hours, calendar days, operating cycles).

attributes.name: interval_value
attributes.description: Numeric value of the maintenance interval (e.g., 5000 for 5000 miles, 100 for 100 engine hours, 365 for 365 days).

attributes.name: last_completed_date
attributes.description: The date when this maintenance service was last completed for the asset.

attributes.name: last_completed_hours
attributes.description: The engine hour meter reading when this maintenance service was last completed. Null if not applicable.

attributes.name: last_completed_mileage
attributes.description: The odometer mileage reading when this maintenance service was last completed. Null if not applicable.

attributes.name: last_modified_by
attributes.description: Username or identifier of the user who last modified this maintenance schedule record.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this maintenance schedule record was last updated in the system.

attributes.name: lead_time_days
attributes.description: Number of days advance notice required before the scheduled maintenance due date to allow for planning, parts procurement, and resource allocation.

attributes.name: next_due_date
attributes.description: The calendar date by which the next scheduled maintenance service must be completed. Null if trigger basis is not calendar-based.

attributes.name: next_due_hours
attributes.description: The engine hour meter reading at which the next scheduled maintenance service is due. Null if trigger basis is not engine hours or flight hours.

attributes.name: next_due_mileage
attributes.description: The odometer mileage reading at which the next scheduled maintenance service is due. Null if trigger basis is not mileage.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, special instructions, or comments related to this maintenance schedule.

attributes.name: parts_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether replacement parts or consumables are required for this maintenance service (True) or if it is inspection/labor only (False).

attributes.name: priority_level
attributes.description: Business priority level assigned to this maintenance schedule based on asset criticality and operational impact.

attributes.name: regulation_reference
attributes.description: Specific regulation, code section, or standard that mandates this maintenance schedule (e.g., 49 CFR 396.17, ICAO Annex 6 Part I, IMO SOLAS Chapter II-1).
attributes.references: US DOT FMCSA Regulations, ICAO Annex 6, IMO SOLAS

attributes.name: regulatory_body
attributes.description: The governing regulatory body that mandates this maintenance requirement (DOT, ICAO, IMO, FAA, FMCSA, EASA, IATA). Null if not compliance-driven. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: DOT|ICAO|IMO|FAA|FMCSA|EASA|IATA — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: US DOT, ICAO, IMO, FAA, FMCSA, EASA, IATA

attributes.name: schedule_effective_date
attributes.description: The date from which this maintenance schedule becomes active and applicable to the asset.

attributes.name: schedule_expiry_date
attributes.description: The date on which this maintenance schedule is no longer applicable (e.g., asset retirement, schedule superseded by new regulation). Null for open-ended schedules.

attributes.name: schedule_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the maintenance schedule (active, suspended, completed, overdue, cancelled).

attributes.name: service_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of the maintenance service activities and scope of work included in this schedule.

attributes.name: service_type
attributes.description: Type of preventive maintenance service defined in this schedule (e.g., oil change, tire rotation, brake inspection, DOT annual inspection, ICAO 100-hour check, engine overhaul).
attributes.references: US DOT FMCSA Regulations, ICAO Annex 6

attributes.name: tolerance_after_days
attributes.description: Number of days after the due date that the maintenance service may be performed late before the asset is considered non-compliant or overdue.
attributes.references: US DOT FMCSA Regulations, ICAO Annex 6

attributes.name: tolerance_before_days
attributes.description: Number of days before the due date that the maintenance service may be performed early without resetting the schedule interval.

attributes.name: trigger_basis
attributes.description: The measurement basis that triggers this maintenance service (mileage interval, engine hours, calendar days, flight hours, operating cycles).

products.name: fuel_transaction
products.description: Transactional record capturing every fuel uplift and energy consumption event for fleet assets. Tracks asset reference, driver reference, transaction datetime, fuel station/depot location, fuel type (diesel, petrol, LNG, SAF — Sustainable Aviation Fuel, electric charge), quantity (litres or kWh), unit cost, total cost, odometer reading at fill, fuel card number, supplier reference, and CO2e emission factor applied. Feeds sustainability domain for GHG reporting under EU ETS and CORSIA, and finance domain for OPEX fuel cost allocation.

attributes.name: supplier_id

attributes.name: transport_asset_id

attributes.name: trip_id

attributes.name: authorization_code

attributes.name: co2e_emission_factor

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this fuel transaction record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the transaction amount (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP).

attributes.name: discount_amount
attributes.description: Discount or rebate amount applied to the transaction based on supplier agreements or fuel card programs.

attributes.name: fuel_card_number

attributes.name: fuel_card_provider

attributes.name: fuel_efficiency

attributes.name: fuel_grade

attributes.name: fuel_station_country_code

attributes.name: fuel_station_location

attributes.name: fuel_station_name
attributes.description: Name of the fuel station, depot, or charging facility where the transaction took place.

attributes.name: fuel_type
attributes.description: Type of fuel or energy consumed. Includes diesel, petrol (gasoline), LNG (Liquefied Natural Gas), CNG (Compressed Natural Gas), SAF (Sustainable Aviation Fuel), electric charge, hydrogen, or biodiesel. Critical for sustainability and emissions reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: diesel|petrol|lng|cng|saf|electric|hydrogen|biodiesel — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Energy Classification Standard, CORSIA, EU ETS

attributes.name: general_ledger_account
attributes.description: General ledger account code for fuel expense posting. Used for financial accounting and P&L reporting.

attributes.name: is_emergency_refuel
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this was an emergency or unplanned refueling event outside of normal depot operations. Used for exception analysis.

attributes.name: is_reconciled
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this transaction has been reconciled with supplier invoices and financial records.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this fuel transaction record was last modified. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes or comments about the fuel transaction. May include driver remarks, exception explanations, or audit notes.

attributes.name: odometer_reading
attributes.description: Odometer or hour-meter reading of the asset at the time of fuel uplift. Used for fuel efficiency analysis and maintenance scheduling.

attributes.name: odometer_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the odometer reading (kilometers, miles, or operating hours for aircraft/vessels).

attributes.name: payment_method
attributes.description: Method of payment used for the fuel transaction (fuel card, credit card, cash, invoice, direct debit).

attributes.name: quantity
attributes.description: Quantity of fuel or energy consumed in the transaction. Measured in litres for liquid fuels or kWh for electric charging.

attributes.name: reconciliation_date
attributes.description: Date when the transaction was reconciled with supplier invoices and approved for payment.

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Name of the source system or fuel card provider system from which this transaction was captured (e.g., SAP TM, fuel card provider API, telematics system).

attributes.name: supplier_invoice_number
attributes.description: Invoice number issued by the fuel supplier for this transaction. Used for accounts payable reconciliation.

attributes.name: tax_amount
attributes.description: Total tax amount applied to the fuel transaction. Includes VAT, excise duty, or other applicable fuel taxes.

attributes.name: total_cost
attributes.description: Total cost of the fuel transaction including base fuel cost and any applicable surcharges or taxes. Represents the net amount payable.

attributes.name: transaction_datetime
attributes.description: The date and time when the fuel uplift or energy charge event occurred. Principal business event timestamp.

attributes.name: transaction_number
attributes.description: Externally-known unique transaction number or receipt number issued by the fuel supplier or fuel card provider.

attributes.name: transaction_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the fuel transaction. Indicates whether the transaction has been completed, is pending reconciliation, disputed, cancelled, or reversed.

attributes.name: unit_cost
attributes.description: Cost per unit of fuel or energy (e.g., cost per litre, cost per kWh). Used for cost analysis and budgeting.

attributes.name: unit_of_measure
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the fuel quantity. Typically litres or gallons for liquid fuels, kWh for electric, kg for hydrogen, or m3 for gas.

products.name: asset_inspection
products.description: Transactional record for all formal regulatory and operational inspections conducted on fleet assets. Captures asset reference, inspection type (DOT roadside inspection, ICAO airworthiness check, IMO vessel survey, pre-trip inspection, annual safety inspection, C-TPAT security inspection), inspection date, inspector name/authority, inspection outcome (pass, fail, conditional), defects identified, corrective actions required, reinspection due date, and regulatory certificate issued. Distinct from maintenance_order — inspections are compliance events that may or may not trigger maintenance work.
products.reference: DOT Inspection Report / ICAO Airworthiness Certificate

Inspection certificates must be maintained as evidence of progra

attributes.name: certificate_issue_date

attributes.name: certificate_number

attributes.name: corrective_action_deadline

attributes.name: corrective_actions_required

attributes.name: critical_defects_count

attributes.name: defects_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative description of all defects, non-conformances, and observations identified during the inspection. Includes severity classification and affected components.

attributes.name: defects_identified_count
attributes.description: Total number of defects, non-conformances, or discrepancies identified during the inspection. Zero indicates no issues found.

attributes.name: inspection_checklist_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier for the standardized inspection checklist or procedure document used to conduct this inspection.

attributes.name: inspection_cost
attributes.description: Total cost incurred for conducting the inspection, including labor, materials, third-party fees, and administrative overhead.

attributes.name: inspection_cost_currency
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO currency code for the inspection cost amount.

attributes.name: inspection_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which the inspection was conducted. This is the principal business event timestamp for regulatory compliance and audit purposes.

attributes.name: inspection_document_url
attributes.description: URL or file path to the digital inspection report, certificate scan, or supporting documentation stored in the document management system.

attributes.name: inspection_end_time
attributes.description: Precise timestamp when the inspection was completed. Used to calculate inspection duration and resource utilization.

attributes.name: inspection_location_country
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO country code of the jurisdiction where the inspection took place. Critical for determining applicable regulatory framework.

attributes.name: inspection_notes
attributes.description: Additional free-text notes, observations, or comments recorded by the inspector that provide context beyond structured fields.

attributes.name: inspection_number
attributes.description: Externally-known unique identifier or reference number for this inspection event, often used for regulatory reporting and audit trails.
attributes.references: DOT Inspection Standards, ICAO Annex 8, IMO Resolution A.1120(30)

attributes.name: inspection_outcome
attributes.description: Overall result of the inspection. Pass indicates full compliance; fail indicates critical defects requiring immediate action; conditional pass indicates minor defects with corrective action required within a specified timeframe.
attributes.references: DOT Out-of-Service Criteria, ICAO Airworthiness Standards, IMO Port State Control Guidelines

attributes.name: inspection_start_time
attributes.description: Precise timestamp when the inspection commenced. Used for operational tracking and labor cost allocation.

attributes.name: inspection_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the inspection event. Tracks progression from scheduling through completion or cancellation.

attributes.name: inspection_type
attributes.description: Category of inspection conducted. Determines the regulatory framework, scope, and compliance requirements applicable to this inspection event.
attributes.value_regex: DOT roadside inspection|ICAO airworthiness check|IMO vessel survey|pre-trip inspection|annual safety inspection|C-TPAT security inspection
attributes.references: DOT FMCSA Regulations, ICAO Annex 8, IMO SOLAS Convention, C-TPAT Security Criteria

attributes.name: inspector_authority

attributes.name: inspector_certification_number

attributes.references: DOT Inspector Certification, ICAO Licensing Standards

attributes.name: inspector_name
attributes.description: Full name of the individual who conducted the inspection. May be an internal employee or external regulatory authority representative.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this inspection record was last updated. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: next_inspection_due_date
attributes.description: The date by which the next scheduled inspection of this type must be conducted to maintain regulatory compliance and operational certification.
attributes.references: DOT Inspection Intervals, ICAO Continuing Airworthiness, IMO Survey Schedules

attributes.name: odometer_reading_at_inspection
attributes.description: Odometer or usage meter reading (kilometers, miles, flight hours, engine hours) recorded at the time of inspection. Used for maintenance interval tracking.

attributes.name: out_of_service_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the asset was placed out of service as a result of this inspection due to critical safety defects or regulatory non-compliance.

attributes.name: out_of_service_start_date
attributes.description: The date the asset was officially placed out of service following the inspection. Null if asset was not taken out of service.

attributes.name: regulatory_certificate_issued
attributes.description: Name or type of regulatory certificate, permit, or compliance document issued as a result of passing this inspection (e.g., DOT Annual Inspection Certificate, ICAO Certificate of Airworthiness, IMO Safety Equipment Certificate).

attributes.name: reinspection_due_date

attributes.name: reinspection_required_flag

attributes.name: licence_class
attributes.description: Class designation within the licence category, defining specific operational limits or capabilities (e.g., Class 1 for heavy trucks, Class A for multi-engine aircraft).

attributes.name: licence_fee_amount
attributes.description: Total fee paid to the issuing authority for the issuance or renewal of this licence. Excludes taxes and processing charges.

attributes.name: licence_fee_currency
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the licence fee amount (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP).

attributes.name: licence_number
attributes.description: The official licence, permit, or certificate number issued by the regulatory authority. This is the externally-known unique identifier for the licence.

attributes.name: licence_type
attributes.description: Classification of the licence or permit. Defines the regulatory purpose and scope of the licence (e.g., vehicle registration for road use, airworthiness certificate for aircraft operation, dangerous goods permit for hazardous cargo transport). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: vehicle_registration|operating_licence|airworthiness_certificate|vessel_class_certificate|dangerous_goods_permit|oversize_overweight_permit|cross_border_transit_permit|emission_certificate|insurance_certificate|roadworthiness_certificate — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: next_inspection_due_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next mandatory inspection or audit required to maintain licence validity. Null if no future inspection is scheduled.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional comments, special conditions, or operational notes related to this licence (e.g., pending appeal, conditional approval, temporary exemption granted).

attributes.name: payment_reference
attributes.description: Payment transaction reference or receipt number for the licence fee payment. Used for audit and reconciliation purposes.

attributes.name: regulatory_reference
attributes.description: Citation of the specific regulation, statute, or legal framework under which this licence is issued (e.g., 49 CFR Part 383, ICAO Annex 8, SOLAS Chapter II-1).

attributes.name: renewal_due_date
attributes.description: Target date by which the licence renewal process must be initiated to avoid lapse. Typically set ahead of expiry_date to allow processing time.

attributes.name: renewal_reminder_days
attributes.description: Number of days before expiry_date when automated renewal reminders should be triggered to fleet managers and compliance officers.

attributes.name: responsible_party
attributes.description: Name or employee ID of the fleet manager, compliance officer, or department responsible for managing and renewing this licence.

attributes.name: validity_status
attributes.description: Current validity state of the licence. Indicates whether the asset is legally compliant to operate under this licence. Valid = currently active and compliant; Expired = past expiry date; Suspended = temporarily invalid; Revoked = permanently cancelled; Pending Renewal = renewal application submitted; Pending Approval = initial application under review.

products.name: incident
products.description: Transactional record capturing all fleet-related incidents including road accidents, near-misses, cargo damage events, vehicle breakdowns, and security incidents. Tracks incident datetime, location (GPS coordinates and address), asset reference, driver reference, incident type, severity classification, third-party involvement flag, police report number, injuries reported, estimated asset damage cost, cargo damage reference, insurance claim reference, root cause classification, and corrective action status. Feeds the claim domain for cargo insurance processing and supports DOT accident reporting obligations.
products.reference: DOT Accident Report / IATA Safety Occurrence Report

attributes.name: incident_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the fleet incident record. Primary key.

attributes.name: asset_assignment_id

attributes.name: cargo_claim_id
attributes.description: Reference to the insurance claim filed for this incident (if applicable). Links to the claim domain for processing.

attributes.name: carrier_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to network.carrier. Business justification: Incidents involving contracted carrier assets or drivers require carrier linkage for liability determination, insurance claims processing, carrier performance impact assessment, and regulatory reporti

attributes.name: consignment_id
attributes.description: Reference to the shipment being transported at the time of the incident (if applicable). Links to cargo damage claims.

attributes.name: customs_declaration_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to customs.declaration. Business justification: Incidents during cross-border transport (accidents, cargo damage, theft) must be reported in relation to customs declarations for insurance claims, duty adjustments, and regulatory investigations. Req

attributes.name: driver_profile_id
attributes.description: Reference to the driver or operator assigned to the asset at the time of the incident.

attributes.name: facility_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to warehouse.facility. Business justification: Incidents occurring at warehouse facilities must be linked to the facility for safety reporting, insurance claim processing, and regulatory compliance (OSHA/DOT). Facility-level incident tracking is r
